explanation: Direct eye contact is valued in Italy as a sign of sincerity, confidence, and engagement, especially during greetings and business meetings. It's standard practice during introductions and conversations, and avoiding it can come across as evasive or disinterested.
local_tip: Hold a steady, friendly gaze during greetings and conversation, without staring fixedly.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact can be seen as intimidating; brief glances are preferred.
Direct eye contact is valued as a sign of honesty, typically less intense than in Italy.
Sustained eye contact with a superior may be seen as challenging; juniors often lower their gaze.

sources.title: Business Culture Around the World: Italy
